subslides.chapter: Euclidean Law of Cosines (acute): c² + 2ap = a² + b²
subslides.symbolic: c² + 2a·p = a² + b²  (p = b cos B)
subslides.clause_html:
Euclidean Law of Cosines (Acute)
c² + 2a·p = a² + b² ⇔ c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos B
Holds for the side opposite any acute angle in any triangle (acute, right, or obtuse), completing with I.47 and II.12 the metric theory of triangles.
subslides.just_title: Noted by the Greek scholiast (Heiberg Vol. V, p. 253), Campanus, and Clavius; Heron proved the converse via I.25.
